Sprint Zero · worked example · ghost-lite

What got built, and how we tested it

One command, four sub-agents, six specification documents, and a running publishing app that answers questions from Hamza's own blog posts. This is the record of the run, including the parts that stalled.

Run: 10 to 11 September 2026 Reference: ghost.org · TryGhost/Ghost Seed: blog.traversaal.ai

The ask

Reverse-engineer Ghost, add the one thing it lacks

Ghost is the open-source publishing platform: 55,000 GitHub stars, MIT licensed, the thing Hamza's own blog runs on. Sprint Zero was pointed at it with one instruction that Ghost does not have: Ask me, a question box on every site that answers from the site's own posts and cites them.

The scope was MVP: real signup and login, real rows in a database, one core loop working end to end. Stack: Express and React on a local SQLite file, so a fresh clone runs with no accounts and no keys. Fifteen things were excluded on purpose, from paid tiers to comments to a rich editor, so the agents could not wander.

Instead of invented filler, the seed is real: the ten most recent articles from the Traversaal.ai blog, pulled from its RSS feed the morning of the run, with the blog's own title, description, and accent color #fc654a.

The app

Two engineers built in parallel from the contract without seeing each other's code. The backend is Express 5 with better-sqlite3, a self-issued JWT, and an FTS5 full-text index that holds only published posts. The frontend is React 18 on Vite, plain JavaScript, with markdown rendered through a sanitiser. Forty-two source files, about 2,900 lines.

The public side follows Ghost's Casper theme, measured from the live demo: the site's accent paints the cover and the header bar, titles are set at weight 800, post bodies in Georgia at 20px on a 720px reading column, a 48px Subscribe pill, a black footer. The writer's admin follows Ghost's Shade look: white, one pale sidebar, 13px UI text, black buttons.

How Ask me works

Retrieval is SQLite's FTS5 over the title and body of published posts, inside the same database file as everything else. Draft posts are never in the index. The reader's question is reduced to quoted tokens joined with OR, so quotes, parentheses, and FTS operators typed by a reader are inert.

What happens next depends on one environment variable. With no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, the box returns the top five matching posts with highlighted passages and labels them Search results. With a key, the server hands the matching passages to Claude (claude-opus-5, 12-second timeout), instructed to answer only from them and to say when they do not cover the question, and returns the written answer labelled Answer with citations filtered to posts that were actually retrieved.

Three rules keep it honest. If nothing matches, the model is never called and the reader sees "No matches". If the model call fails or times out, the reader gets the passages plus a note that an answer could not be written, never an error page. And no citation can point at a post that was not in the results.

A fix after QA. The first live answer was honest but thin: the backend passed the model only the short highlighted snippet per post, a heading fragment of about sixty tokens, and the model correctly said the passages did not explain the concept. The backend engineer was re-spawned to hand the model the matching paragraphs (1,200 to 1,800 characters per post) while leaving the response shape untouched. The tests were re-run after. After the fix, the same question returns a real definition with a citation to the context-engineering article, and a question about self-hosting returns the blog's actual thresholds with two citations. The integration suite still passes, 102 of 102.

Part two

How we tested it

A separate QA agent read both codebases against the contract, wrote an integration test file, then drove the running app in a real browser. It fixed nothing in the application code, because nothing needed fixing. This is its report, restated.

What the integration test actually does

One standalone Node script, 347 lines, run with node tests/integration.test.js from server/ against a live server. It exits non-zero on any failure and reads only the presence of a key from the environment, never its value. It walks: health; signup, duplicate signup, login, wrong password; site create and edit; post create, edit, publish, unpublish, delete, with the publish-date and slug invariants; public reads and the draft 404; members with a mixed-case email; and Ask me with a normal question, a no-match question, a punctuation-hostile question, and a deliberately malformed FTS expression.

The browser pass, step by step

  1. Open the landing page. Click the hero call to action. Sign up with a fresh timestamped email.
  2. Land on site setup. Create "Field Notes" with a green accent. Confirm the dashboard shows the site name.
  3. Create a draft titled "On mulch". Publish it. Confirm the status label reads Published and the post appears on the public site and its own page.
  4. Create a second draft, "Compost secrets", containing the phrase "zebrafish quantum marmalade". Leave it unpublished.
  5. As an anonymous reader, open /s/traversaal-ai. Confirm the cover computes to rgb(252, 101, 74), ten cards newest first, the MLOps post renders markdown with no script tags.
  6. Join with " QA@Example.com ". Confirm "now a member". Join again. Confirm "already a member".
  7. Ask "what is progressive disclosure in context engineering?" Confirm the label and the first result. Ask "how do I bake sourdough?" Confirm "No matches". Ask about zebrafish. Confirm nothing leaks.
  8. Log out. Confirm the token is cleared and the landing page shows the login link. Log in again. Overwrite the stored token with "expired". Reload. Confirm the 401 redirect.
  9. Restart the server with a real key. Repeat the progressive-disclosure question. Confirm "Answer" and a citation link. Restart with an invalid key. Confirm the degradation note.

What we did not test, and what we noticed

  • The member feed (a signed-in reader's list of posts across sites) was deferred by the contract with a stated reason: members have no login, so there is nothing to sign into. Not tested, not built.
  • Error-path browser tests belong to Prod scope. Not run.
  • Search-mode snippets can show raw markdown (a ## heading, an image's alt text) because the contract specifies snippets over the stored markdown. A content-polish item, not a contract issue.
  • One model call in answer mode, on the punctuation-hostile question, hit the 12-second timeout and degraded correctly to passages.
  • The seed's completion log says "N published posts" but counts all statuses. Cosmetic.
  • The first backend engineer session stalled for ten minutes during its own verification, after writing about 1,000 lines. The kit's checkpoint file recorded it as running, a second session was spawned to verify what existed, and it passed with no code changes. That resume path is now part of the kit.

Try it

Run it yourself

No accounts, no keys. Two terminals.

# terminal 1
cd server && npm install && node seed.js && node index.js      # :3001

# terminal 2
cd client && npm install && npm run dev                          # :5173

# optional: let Ask me write answers instead of listing passages
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=...   # before starting the server

Demo login: demo@traversaal.ai / inkwell-demo. Public site: http://localhost:5173/s/traversaal-ai.

The ten-minute class demo

  1. Open the presenter. Show the Live tab: ten steps, six clickable docs, QA green. Open api-contract.md and read the Ask me endpoint aloud.
  2. Open the site. Point out the cover color is the blog's real accent, the ten posts are real, and the footer says Powered by Ghost because the theme was measured, not guessed.
  3. Ask "when does self-hosting an LLM pay off?" Read the answer. Click the citation.
  4. Sign in as the demo writer. Publish a two-line post. Ask a question only that post can answer. Watch it get cited.
  5. Stop the server, start it without the key. Ask again. Show the same box returning passages instead, with the honest label.
  6. Open server/tests/integration.test.js. Run it. Watch the count.
Reference: Ghost, by the Ghost Foundation, MIT licensed. Seed content: ten articles by Hamza Farooq from blog.traversaal.ai, itself a Ghost site. Hero photograph: Markus Winkler on Pexels. Every specification document and every line of application code in this record was produced by the Sprint Zero pipeline; nothing was authored by hand to look like a run.
